definitions.explanation: forcing out or eliminating something completely, often enemies, pests, or unwanted elements

examples.japanese: {害虫|がいちゅう}を{駆逐|くちく}する。
{悪習|あくしゅう}を{駆逐|くちく}することが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It is important to root out bad habits.

examples.japanese: その{新製品|しんせいひん}は{従来|じゅうらい}の{製品|せいひん}を{市場|しじょう}から{駆逐|くちく}した。
examples.english: That new product drove the conventional products out of the market.

notes:
{駆逐|くちく} means to drive out or eradicate, used for eliminating enemies, pests, or unwanted things.

KANJI BREAKDOWN:
- {駆|く} (drive, gallop)
- {逐|ちく} (pursue, chase)

USAGE:
- {駆逐|くちく}する (to eradicate - suru verb)
- 〜を{駆逐|くちく}する (to drive out ~)

COMMON OBJECTS:
- {敵|てき}を{駆逐|くちく}する (to rout the enemy)
- {害虫|がいちゅう}を{駆逐|くちく}する (to eradicate pests)
- {悪習|あくしゅう}を{駆逐|くちく}する (to root out bad habits)
- {競合|きょうごう}を{駆逐|くちく}する (to drive out competitors)

MILITARY TERM:
- {駆逐艦|くちくかん} (destroyer - naval vessel)
- Originally meant a ship designed to "destroy" torpedo boats

FORMALITY:
- Formal/written style
- Common in news, business, military contexts

RELATED TERMS:
- {排除|はいじょ} (exclusion, elimination)
- {追|お}い{払|はら}う (to drive away)
- {撲滅|ぼくめつ} (eradication, extermination)
